To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a signal vector of narrowband signals can be decomposed to a set of subbands in order to separate their spectra from the noise spectra and that the proposed blind source separation technique can provide an accurate estimate of the second statistics of the subband signal vectors.
a novel approach to second order statistics based blind signal source separation is proposed.

(1) the subband technique provides an unbiased estimate of second order statistics of noisy observed signal vectors, (2) the subband based blind source separation algorithm provides high efficiency and usefulness for the blind separation of narrowband sources of interest from narrowband colored noise, and (3) the proposed blind source separation approach is applicable to the separation of narrowband speech sources from colored noise, which is a common situation in many real world applications
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new technique for separating the spectra of the source signals in a noisy observed signal using a bank of filters.
the development of new algorithms for blind source separation of signals of interest in the presence of additive noise of which the frequency of its spectral peaks is either known or can estimated.
the blind separation of a mixture of narrowband signals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed approach provides an efficient solution to blind separation of narrowband noisy observed signals.
the proposed blind source separation approach is a very promising alternative to the existing approaches for blind source separation of noisy observed signal vectors.
the proposed subband technique is a powerful approach for blind source separation of noisy observed signal vectors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that the second order statistics based blind separation of the subbands of a signal vector can provide an effective and efficient solution for blind separation of signals in colored noise.
the proposed subband technique is able to improve the separation performance in the presence of additive colored noise, which is a significant contribution in the field of blind source separation.
we have successfully developed a new approach for blind source separation of signals in additive colored noise using second order statistics and a bank of subbands.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the subband decomposition technique is a powerful tool to enhance the performance of the blind source separation algorithms in the presence of noise.
a blind source separation algorithm can be designed based on the second order statistics using a bank of narrowband filters.

the proposed approach can be applied to any signal processing task that requires the second order statistics (e.g. spectral estimation, blind deconvolution, etc.) of a noisy observed vector of signals.
